record.question: Don't just waste money on whatever you want. Pick out the correct clause of the underlined words.
record.explanation: Answer A: noun clause. The underlined “whatever you want” is an embedded interrogative clause functioning as the object of “on”, so it is nominal/noun clause. Independent check: “Whatever you want” is the complement of the preposition “on”; in traditional terms it is a noun clause. Reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/clauses. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Exact printed question, choices and required directions/emphasis reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
